subject: Post-call technical recap & next steps — MetalLex inference qualification
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex@metallex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call technical recap & next steps — MetalLex inference qualification

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we all have the same priorities and next steps. I've kept this focused on the technical constraints you raised and the immediate follow-ups from our side.

Summary of pain points you mentioned:
- High tail latency during bursty traffic (notable p95 spikes during 10–15 minute windows)
- Cost sensitivity at sustained throughput — need to balance quality with per-token/unit economics
- Regulatory requirement: customer PII must remain in US-only regions and be encrypted at rest
- Desire to run a fine-tuned Llama2-13B variant and evaluate performance vs. a quantized open model

Goals we aligned on:
1) Validate a deployment topology that meets latency SLOs and data residency requirements.
2) Produce an initial capacity plan for your 30–75 concurrent requests baseline and 150 concurrent peak (burst) profile.
3) Share a short list of recommended instance/GPU configurations and an expected latency/throughput envelope for each.
4) Get SOC2 & procurement questionnaire items surfaced to your security/procurement teams.

Initial technical targets we discussed (for qualification):
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for 512-token prompts during normal load; p95 <= 300ms during controlled bursts with autoscale/fallback.
- Throughput: sustain 800 req/min with 30–75 concurrency baseline; support 9k req/hr bursts with autoscale.
- Model footprint: Llama2-13B (fine-tuned) quantized to int8 or int4 where possible; fallback to 13B FP16 for quality runs.

Proposed next steps (owners + dates):
- Sean: deliver a short topology proposal and capacity estimate by 2028-11-17 (attachment: metallex_slo_requirements.xlsx).
- Karthik: provide a hardware-performance sketch (H100 vs A100 vs T4 cost/latency tradeoffs) by 2028-11-20.
- Alex: share procurement timeline and any compliance docs (SOC2 evidence, legal contacts).
- Marissa: schedule a 45-min compliance + security follow-up with MetalLex security (target week of 2028-11-27).

Notes about approach we recommended on the call:
- Dedicated pool in a US region (us-east-1) for PII workloads; private control plane if you want VPC-only access.
- Prefix KV caching for repeated prompts to cut token generation cost and reduce tail latency.
- Canary rollout of the fine-tuned model (A/B with quantized variant) with automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant under load.

Attachments: metallex_slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub — SLO matrix & traffic samples).

If I've missed anything or a number above needs to be adjusted, flag it and I'll update. Happy to hop on a short follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

—Sean

Sean — really helpful, thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and constraints from our side that will affect the topology: 

- Data residency: everything must live in US regions only; any backup/archives also need to remain in-region.
- SOC2: we are SOC2 Type II in scope and will require evidence for logging/audit trails and key management.
- Security: KMS integration is required (we use AWS KMS).
- Throughput reality check: our expected continuous concurrency is closer to 25–40, but we do see short spikes up to ~120 concurrent requests during end-of-day processing windows.
- Model: we will initially move our fine-tuned Llama2-13B model. If quantized variants are within ~3% quality delta we’re open to int8/in4 for cost savings, but we need accuracy benchmarks.

Questions for Redwood engineering: 
1) Can you bucket expected p95 latency by hardware target (H100, A100, T4) for both FP16 and int8 quantized variants? Please include cold-start vs warm-cache numbers if possible.
2) How do you handle KV cache invalidation across canaries/rollouts?
3) For bursts where autoscale is catching up, what are the recommended fallback policies (queueing, degraded sampling, model-fallback order)?

I attached an initial procurement PDF (procurement-initial.pdf) and our security point-of-contact is ella.kim@metallex.com — copy her on the SOC2 requests.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the topology doc.

—Alex
Alex Romero
Head of AI Platform, MetalLex, Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-11-16T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Technical deep-dive — proposed topology & performance sketch for MetalLex

Alex / team — following on Sean's summary, I sketched a practical topology and perf envelope based on the traffic profile you gave. High-level proposal below; I attached a one-page topology diagram (metallex_inference_topology_diagram.pdf).

Topology (recommended for US-only, PII workloads):
- Dedicated Redwood Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 with reserved GPU pool.
  - Baseline capacity: 2 x H100 (reserved) to satisfy steady-state testing; burst pool: autoscale to add up to 4 additional H100s for peak.
  - Alternative cost tier: 4 x A100 (train-grade) or 6 x T4 for lower cost profile; we can provide latency tradeoffs for each.
- Private control plane + VPC peering into MetalLex VPC for data ingress/egress; AWS KMS integration for envelope encryption of model artifacts and logs.
- KV cache layer in-memory colocated with the serving nodes (prefix cache + configurable TTL) to accelerate repeated prompts.
- Ingress routing: smart-router that directs traffic by SLO policy: (latency-sensitive -> reserved pool) | (best-effort -> burst/cost-efficient pool).

Performance sketch (ballpark numbers for Llama2-13B family):
- H100 (FP16): warm p50 ~ 28–35ms per token; p95 warm for 512-token prompt ~ 120–160ms depending on batching. Cold start adds ~80–150ms for model spin-up if not kept warm.
- H100 (int8 quantized): warm p95 for 512 tokens ~ 80–110ms; quality delta typically < 3% for many classification/assistant tasks but depends on your fine-tuning.
- A100 (FP16): warm p95 ~ 140–200ms for 512 tokens; int8 benefits similar but slightly worse than H100.
- T4 (int8): cost-effective for low-concurrency workloads; expect p95 ~ 250–400ms on 512 tokens.

Workload management & SLO preservation strategies:
- Continuous batching with dynamic batch size cap (we typically start with cap=8–16 for low-latency configs).
- Prefix KV caching to collapse repeated prefixes — we observed up to 35–50% token compute reduction in similar customers.
- Circuit-breaker + degraded-mode policy: if queue > X ms, route to quantized model or reduce sampling length/temperature to protect tails.
- Canary & rollout: KV cache namespacing + canary-tagged cache entries to avoid cross-traffic contamination. On fail, automatic rollback to previous model or fallback to an open 7B variant.

Next artifacts we will deliver:
- Detailed capacity spreadsheet with cost estimates for H100 / A100 / T4 by 2028-11-20 (Karthik).
- Benchmark plan: short synthetic + representative prompt set run on your fine-tuned artifact (you'll provide model + sample prompt set). We recommend an initial 48-hour soak test during a non-production window.

Security/compliance notes:
- We'll provide audit log samples and KMS integration guide for SOC2 review.
- For on-prem/air-gapped needs we can discuss Redwood Private later in procurement if required.

Open questions from the engineering side:
- Can MetalLex provide a representative 500–1,000 prompt samples and an expected token distribution?
- Are there specific blackout windows for scale testing?

I'll follow up with the topology PDF and a HubSpot note linking the capacity sheet.

—Karthik
